tagline: Lonely roads from Chaco Canyon to a rock full of names.
intro: Chaco Canyon sits at the middle of this web of roads, a remote canyon cut by the Chaco Wash. South of the park the road crosses lonely country, then winds among sandstone buttes near Crownpoint, where a Navajo rug auction comes round once a month. Farther west, El Morro appears on the horizon like an ocean liner.

North, around Farmington, there was water, and people settled there early. Two Chacoan outlier pueblos of the eleventh century are open to visitors. West of town US 64 runs down a canyon of yellow- and gray-striped hills toward Arizona.

moments.title: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
moments.text: Between 900 and 1150 the Chacoans hauled timber from great distances to raise 15 major complexes here, the largest buildings in North America until the 19th century.

moments.title: El Morro National Monument
moments.text: Above a pool at the foot of the bluff travelers carved their names for centuries, the oldest legible one Juan de Oñate's of April 16, 1605, until carving was outlawed in 1906.

moments.title: Aztec Ruins National Monument
moments.text: Pueblo ruins on the west bank of the Animas River, named by 19th-century settlers who guessed wrong about who built them.
